paper.quote: Only when there are no more low-priority requests, QoServe proactively relegates high-priority requests that have violated their deadlines to prevent cascading deadline violations.

analysis.tier_note: the reading and the probes disagree
analysis.reasoning: The shown scheduler loop applies eager relegation based solely on deadline slack and drop count; it never checks seq.priority or seq.tier before relegating. Sequence initializes priority to a constant 1 and assigns tiers randomly, but the scheduler snippet has no low-priority-exhaustion gate. Thus the evidence supports the claim that this path treats requests uniformly by deadline.
analysis.would_confirm: A unit test with mixed tiers and an exhausted low-priority queue would show whether high-priority requests are relegated only after low-priority exhaustion.

probes.meaning: Scheduler never reads request priority; control shows drop logic present.
Scheduler never consults tier; control shows deadline field used.
No tier-deadline gating in scheduler; control shows throughput logic present.
Priority is initialized to a constant, not differentiated per request.
